title: Design a Movie Ticket Booking System (BookMyShow)
relevance: High — hard concurrency LLD / machine-coding staple (campus + SDE-2); Flipkart, Swiggy, Amazon, Walmart, Razorpay, BookMyShow-style loops probe seat locking + payment; pairs with HLD Ticketmaster/BookMyShow (hq11).
company_notes: Very common campus/machine-coding BookMyShow LLD at Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Amazon new-grad, and Indian product cos (working hold+confirm + clean classes beat a pattern zoo; concurrency often a stretch after happy path); SDE-2/experienced at FAANG-adjacent, Razorpay, Walmart, BookMyShow expects TTL locks, multi-seat atomicity, and payment failure paths from the start and may bridge to HLD (Redis, waiting room); among the top ~10 hard LLD problems and the canonical concurrency + inventory OOD question after Parking Lot / Elevator.

phases.goal: Clarify scope and lock functional/non-functional requirements, use cases, and demo assumptions before modeling.

must_hit.point: Clarify first: single cinema vs multi-city aggregator, specific seat pick vs auto-assign, seat tiers/pricing, payment in scope, cancel/refund, hold TTL, and whether concurrency is required.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Asks multi-city vs single cinema, seat selection model, pricing, payment, cancel/refund, hold TTL, and concurrency before designing.

must_hit.point: Typical FR: search movies/shows by city (+ title); list cinemas/shows; view seat map; select N seats; temporarily lock; pay; confirm booking; cancel confirmed booking (release seats).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists search/list/map/select/lock/pay/confirm/cancel as the customer path.

must_hit.point: Cover use cases: browse→pay→ticket; two users race same seat → exactly one wins; abandon checkout → TTL frees seats; payment fails → unlock; cancel → seats AVAILABLE again.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks race, TTL abandon, payment-fail unlock, and cancel release—not only the happy path.

must_hit.point: NFR: no double-booking; thread-safe under concurrent holds; extensible pricing/payment; lock TTL; modular services (not one god class).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States no double-booking, concurrent-hold safety, swappable pricing/payment, TTL, and modular services.

must_hit.point: State assumptions for LLD: e.g. one city demo, ~100–300 seats/screen, hold = 10 min, payment mocked, in-memory OK; park UI rendering, real PGW, refunds, waitlist, partner APIs, flash-sale waiting room until asked.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives seat-count/TTL/mock-payment assumptions and parks HLD-only extras until asked.

probes: Before drawing classes, what would you clarify for scope, FRs, NFRs, and assumptions?
Which use cases must work on day one—especially races, abandon, and payment failure?

hints.1: Start with clarifying questions: city scope, seat pick, payment, TTL, concurrency.
hints.2: Separate typical FR (search→lock→pay→confirm/cancel) from NFRs (no double-book, TTL, extensible strategies) and out-of-scope HLD items.
hints.3: Say: clarify multi-city/payment/TTL; FR search/list/map/hold/pay/confirm/cancel; NFR no double-book + concurrent holds; assume ~100–300 seats/screen, 10 min hold, mocked payment; park PGW/waitlist/waiting room.

phases.goal: Establish the city→show hierarchy, ShowSeat inventory, and seat/booking status model.

must_hit.point: Hierarchy: City → Cinema → Screen → Show (movie + screen + startTime) → per-show seat inventory; seat map template on Screen, availability per Show.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws City/Cinema/Screen/Show and says availability is per show, not shared across the day’s shows.

must_hit.point: Seat = layout (row, col, type); racing inventory is ShowSeat / status keyed by (showId, seatId)—mutating one shared Seat.status across shows is wrong.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates layout Seat from per-show ShowSeat inventory and rejects a single shared Seat.status.

must_hit.point: 3-state seat model: AVAILABLE → LOCKED/HELD → BOOKED; never jump AVAILABLE→BOOKED while payment is in flight.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names AVAILABLE/LOCKED|HELD/BOOKED and forbids booking without a hold during payment.

must_hit.point: Booking holds id, user, show, seats, amount, status PENDING|CONFIRMED|CANCELLED, and payment; User 1──* Booking.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists Booking fields and PENDING/CONFIRMED/CANCELLED lifecycle tied to a user.

probes: What is the entity hierarchy from city down to seats, and where does availability live?
How do Seat and ShowSeat differ, and what statuses can a show seat take?

hints.1: Don’t flatten—name City, Cinema, Screen, Show, and seats.
hints.2: Layout on Screen; inventory status per Show; seats move AVAILABLE→LOCKED→BOOKED.
hints.3: City→Cinema→Screen→Show; Seat is row/col/type; ShowSeat status by (showId,seatId); Booking PENDING|CONFIRMED|CANCELLED.

phases.goal: Sketch Facade/Singleton service, SeatLockManager, strategies, and booking construction before coding.

must_hit.point: MovieBookingService as Singleton/Facade over catalog maps plus seatLockManager and bookingManager; APIs findShows / bookTickets or holdSeats+confirmBooking / cancelBooking / admin add*.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows a thin facade service with catalog maps, lock manager, booking manager, and book/hold/confirm/cancel entry points.

must_hit.point: SeatLockManager owns lockedSeats map and TTL scheduler; lockSeats(show, seats, userId) and unlockSeats only if same user and still LOCKED.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names SeatLockManager with TTL unlock and same-user unlock rules.

must_hit.point: PricingStrategy (Weekday/Weekend/Category) and PaymentStrategy (Card/Upi) as interfaces; BookingBuilder for multi-field Booking.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Points Strategy for pricing and payment plus Builder for Booking.

must_hit.point: Optional MovieObserver for new-show alerts; enums SeatType, SeatStatus, BookingStatus, PaymentStatus; don’t force Factory unless seat layouts/payment adapters need it.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions optional Observer and enums; avoids unnecessary Factory.

probes: Walk me through your class diagram and who owns lock transitions versus confirm.
Where do Singleton/Facade, Strategy, Builder, and State show up?

hints.1: Start with MovieBookingService as the facade entry.
hints.2: Add SeatLockManager + BookingManager; inject PricingStrategy/PaymentStrategy; Builder for Booking.
hints.3: Facade Singleton service; SeatLockManager alone does AVAILABLE↔LOCKED (+TTL); BookingManager lock→price→pay→confirm; Strategy + BookingBuilder; optional MovieObserver.

phases.goal: Implement two-phase hold/confirm, all-or-nothing multi-seat holds, and the booking orchestration path.

must_hit.point: Two-phase booking: (1) lock/hold seats atomically → Booking(PENDING); (2) on payment success LOCKED→BOOKED and CONFIRMED, else release LOCKED→AVAILABLE on failure/timeout.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes hold→PENDING then confirm or release—not one AVAILABLE→BOOKED leap during payment.

must_hit.point: Atomic multi-seat hold: check all seats available then lock all under one critical section; any conflict fails the whole request with no orphan partial holds.
must_hit.evidence_hint: All-or-nothing check-then-lock; conflict rolls back with no partial holds.

must_hit.point: Prefer holdSeats → confirmBooking / releaseHold APIs when payment is in scope; mock PaymentStrategy.pay(amount); on failure release locks; on success confirm idempotently.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses two-phase APIs, mocked pay, failure unlock, and idempotent confirm.

must_hit.point: SeatLockManager is the only component allowed to transition AVAILABLE↔LOCKED (and timeout release); BookingManager orchestrates lock → price → pay → confirm/release.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Assigns lock transitions to SeatLockManager and orchestration to BookingManager.

must_hit.point: Hot path is O(k) seats under one per-show lock, not a global lock; state knobs like numCities, seatsPerScreen, lockTtlMs rather than HLD capacity math.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says LLD skips capacity math and codes O(k) under a per-show lock.

probes: Walk through hold then confirm when payment is in scope—what happens on success vs failure?
How do you lock multiple seats together without leaving a partial hold?

hints.1: Prefer two-phase over one-shot if payment is in scope.
hints.2: All-or-nothing under one critical section; pay mocked; failure releases.
hints.3: holdSeats→Booking(PENDING); pay; success LOCKED→BOOKED+CONFIRMED else unlock; multi-seat check-all-then-lock-all; SeatLockManager owns AVAILABLE↔LOCKED.

phases.goal: Show Open/Closed plug points for pricing, payment, booking lifecycle, and optional notifications without rewriting the critical section.

must_hit.point: Strategy swaps PricingStrategy (weekday/weekend/category) and PaymentStrategy (card/UPI) without editing the booking flow or critical section.
must_hit.evidence_hint: New pricing/payment is a new strategy class; lock/confirm path unchanged.

must_hit.point: Seat/booking lifecycle as State/FSM (enum fine in machine coding; State objects if transitions explode): PENDING→CONFIRMED and AVAILABLE→LOCKED→BOOKED.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses enum FSM or State objects for seat and booking status transitions.

must_hit.point: Facade keeps bookTickets/findShows thin—hides lock + price + pay + confirm; optional Observer notifies users when a watched movie gets a new show.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Facade hides orchestration; Observer only for new-show alerts if asked.

must_hit.point: Out of scope until asked: UI seat map rendering, real PGW, refunds, waitlist, partner theatre APIs, flash-sale waiting room (HLD/hq11).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Parks UI/PGW/refunds/waitlist/partner APIs/waiting room unless interviewer expands.

probes: How would you add weekend pricing or UPI payment without rewriting the lock path?
What would you leave out of scope for LLD versus push to HLD?

hints.1: Name Strategy for pricing/payment as the main OCP plug.
hints.2: Add State/FSM for statuses and optional Observer; keep Facade thin.
hints.3: New WeekendPricing/UpiPayment implement strategies; enum/State for seat+booking; MovieObserver optional; park PGW/waitlist/waiting room.

phases.goal: Make hold+confirm strongly consistent with correct lock granularity, TTL races, and multi-instance fences.

must_hit.point: Lock granularity: per-show synchronized(show) / ReentrantLock (or Redis key show:{id}) so different shows don’t serialize; never hold a DB row lock for the entire payment window.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Chooses per-show lock and refuses to hold DB locks while the user pays.

must_hit.point: Concurrency checklist: check-then-act under one lock; unlock only if still held by same user; TTL must not release BOOKED seats; ordered lock acquisition if locking seat-by-seat (deadlock).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Covers atomic check-then-act, same-user unlock, TTL vs BOOKED, and ordered seat locks.

must_hit.point: ConcurrentHashMap is fine for catalog maps; seat check-then-act still needs an explicit critical section / atomic status transition.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects ConcurrentHashMap alone as sufficient for seat inventory races.

must_hit.point: Search/browse can be eventually consistent; hold+confirm must be strongly consistent; confirm path conditional so late payment can’t overwrite BOOKED or steal an expired hold; unlock only LOCKED→AVAILABLE.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates stale browse from strong hold/confirm and makes confirm/unlock conditional.

must_hit.point: Multi-instance: Redis SET NX PX holds plus conditional DB update / unique (show_id, seat_id) booking constraint as final fence; Redlock alone is not a correctness fence (Kleppmann).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Pairs Redis TTL hold with DB as source of truth and refuses Redlock-alone claims.

probes: Two users click the same seats at once—how do you ensure exactly one wins?
Is ConcurrentHashMap enough for seats, and what changes if you run multiple app instances?

hints.1: Name the race: check-then-act on seat status under a lock.
hints.2: Prefer per-show lock + same-user TTL unlock; CHM only for catalogs.
hints.3: synchronized(show) all-or-nothing hold; unlock only same user + still LOCKED; TTL skips BOOKED; multi-instance Redis NX PX + DB conditional/unique constraint—not Redlock alone.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: One-shot bookTickets is simpler for demos; two-phase hold then confirm is what real ticketing does and what concurrency follow-ups expect when payment is in scope.

tradeoffs.topic: Per-show lock vs per-seat locks vs DB FOR UPDATE
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Per-show lock is simple and correct for LLD; per-seat gives more parallelism but needs ordered seat-id acquisition to avoid deadlock; DB row lock only for a short txn that sets LOCKED+expires_at, never for minutes of user input/payment.
Single JVM: per-show lock + status enum; multi-instance: Redis TTL hold plus conditional DB update / unique (show_id, seat_id) as the final fence—Redis/Redlock alone is not correctness.
Booking conflicts are common on hot shows, so pessimistic / atomic conditional update is preferred; OCC alone causes sad pay-then-fail UX unless you still hold first.

gotchas.trap: Two users click the same seats and both get tickets.
gotchas.correction: Check+lock atomically under a per-show lock (or single conditional multi-row update); loser gets failure/409, not a second ticket.

gotchas.trap: User never pays and seats stay locked forever.
gotchas.correction: TTL/scheduler releases LOCKED→AVAILABLE; unlock must no-op if already BOOKED or held by another user.

gotchas.trap: Payment succeeds twice on retry and double-books or double-charges.
gotchas.correction: Idempotency key / booking id; confirm is conditional on PENDING + held seats.

gotchas.trap: Partial multi-seat success locking only some seats.
gotchas.correction: Forbidden—all-or-nothing hold; rollback on any unavailable seat.

gotchas.trap: Assuming ConcurrentHashMap makes seat booking safe.
gotchas.correction: Fine for catalog maps; seat check-then-act still needs an explicit critical section or atomic status transition.

gotchas.trap: Mutating Screen Seat.status as shared inventory across showtimes.
gotchas.correction: Layout ≠ inventory; materialize status per show (ShowSeat / (showId, seatId)) or you double-sell across showtimes.

gotchas.trap: Claiming Redis Redlock alone makes distributed booking correct.
gotchas.correction: Use Redis SET NX PX for holds plus DB as source of truth (conditional write / unique constraint); don’t claim Redlock alone is a correctness fence.
